battle.name: 潼關之戰
battle.brief: 西魏大統十三年（537）六月，東魏高歡率眾西征，進逼潼關；宇文泰據險深溝高壘，以不足五千之眾當二十萬大軍，七月鐵騎橫蹙渭橋，東魏崩解，棄甲者十餘萬。潼關前線靠槊與環首刀取勝，短劍未曾上陣：卡面羅馬短劍出自東羅馬禁衛軍，作副兵器，其刺擊邏輯與北魏環首刀相通，前線並無此物。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 潼關之戰是北魏一分為二之後，東魏與西魏為爭關中東口而打的一場決戰，交戰年份為西魏大統十三年（537）。東魏建都鄴城，丞相高歡總攝軍政，兵源以河北六鎮降兵與郡縣鄉兵為骨幹，騎兵精悍，軍中號為鐵騎，指揮上高歡坐鎮中軍，前鋒交給彭樂、高敖曹等驍將，翼側與殿後則有斛律金、蔡俊一類宿將，河北大族如渤海高氏、趙郡李氏的部曲多編入騎隊。西魏建都長安，中樞是宇文泰，他出身武川鎮，漢人，位居關隴軍將之首並兼攝相府，本戰前後軍制正逐步收束為柱國與大將分統各部的體制，柱國李弼、趙貴、獨孤信、于謹、侯莫陳崇各領一軍，兵源為關中郡縣軍府兵與六鎮西徙的關隴部曲，步騎兼備而以騎兵為主力，能投入決戰的精騎不過數千。東魏兵多而糧道遠在西魏兵少而據天險，二十萬對數千，攻方靠人海與器械壓上，守方靠地勢與集中一擊，這是全戰最基本的力量對照。
countriesEn: Tong Pass was a decisive engagement fought between the Eastern Wei and the Western Wei for the eastern gateway of Guanzhong, in the thirteenth year of the Datong era, 537, two years after the Northern Wei had split in two. The Eastern Wei, seated at Ye, was ruled in practice by the chancellor Gao Huan, who held the military and civil authority of the state; its troops were recruited chiefly from the surrendered garrisons of the Six Garrisons and from the provincial levies of Hebei, and its cavalry, known as the Tied Cavalry, was the arm that carried its campaigns. Gao Huan sat in the centre of his army and gave the leading role in the assault to such hard riders as Peng Le and Gao Aocao, while veterans such as Hulü Jin and Cai Jun covered the flanks and the rear, and the local households of the great Hebei clans, the Gao of Bohai and the Li of Zhao Commandery, were folded into the mounted contingents. The Western Wei, seated at Chang'an, was directed by Yuwen Tai, a native of Wuchuan, a Han Chinese officer who stood at the head of the Guanzhong commanders and also held the chancellorship; around the time of this battle its military system was being consolidated into a structure in which the pillar lords and the generals each commanded a separate corps. The pillar lords Li Bi, Zhao Gui, Dugu Xin, Yu Jin and Houmo Chen Chong held their own formations, and the Western Wei levies were drawn from the commandery garrisons of Guanzhong and from the migrated households of the Six Garrisons men who had moved west. Their force combined foot and horse, but it was a mounted army above all, and the number of heavy cavalry it could put into the field was no more than a few thousand. The contrast that frames the whole engagement is therefore stark: a host of two hundred thousand against a few thousand, an attacker relying on mass and siege engines, a defender relying on the ground and on a single concentrated blow.
people: 高歡是東魏的實際統帥。他出身渤海高氏，年輕時在爾朱氏麾下效力，六鎮之亂後率兵東走，擁立孝靜帝並遷都鄴城，憑河北軍實與鮮卑騎兵穩住東魏；此戰他志在趁關中饑荒、西魏新立之際，一舉打通蒲津、潼關直取長安。宇文泰是西魏的實際統帥，武川鎮出身，漢人，靠關隴豪族與六鎮降兵的效忠在關中立足，本戰他親至潼關前線，以孤危之地承受東魏大軍。柱國將軍李弼是關中最善戰的謀將，本戰深溝高壘的固守之策與渭橋一線的鐵騎橫蹙皆出其謀；趙貴在關前首當其鋒，以數百騎擊退東魏前鋒；獨孤信、于謹、侯莫陳崇各以本部分據要地，掩護主陣。東魏方面，彭樂受命先鋒，渡橋逼陣，是全場最吃重的攻擊任務；高敖曹為高歡從弟，勇而輕進，渭橋兵敗後收殘卒再戰又潰，與斛律金相遇時勸降不成反險些被斫，最終為部下縛住送京師，兩年後遭誅。斛律金以拒降聞名，是東魏軍中少數在敗局裡仍能維持部伍的將領。
peopleEn: Gao Huan was the overall commander on the Eastern Wei side. He came from the Gao clan of Bohai, had served under the Erzhu regime while young, and after the revolt of the Six Garrisons led his troops east, enthroned Emperor Xiaojing and moved the capital to Ye, holding the Eastern Wei together on the strength of Hebei's manpower and its Xianbei cavalry. In this campaign he meant to exploit the famine in Guanzhong and the new, unsettled state of the Western Wei, break through at Pujin and Tong Pass in one stroke, and take Chang'an. Yuwen Tai was the overall commander on the Western Wei side. A native of Wuchuan and a Han Chinese, he had built his position in Guanzhong on the loyalty of the local gentry and of the men who had fled west from the Six Garrisons, and in this battle he came in person to the front at Tong Pass, holding a single indefensible position against a great army. The pillar lord and general Li Bi was the ablest strategist in Guanzhong: the plan to dig deep and raise high fortifications, and the single stroke of the Tied Cavalry on the Wei Bridge, were both his. Zhao Gui met the first impact of the assault at the pass and turned back the Eastern Wei vanguard with a few hundred riders, while Dugu Xin, Yu Jin and Houmo Chen Chong each held a sector with their own units and covered the main line. On the Eastern Wei side Peng Le was given the task of leading the vanguard, crossing the bridge and pressing the Western Wei position, the heaviest job of the day. Gao Aocao, a cousin of Gao Huan, was brave but rash: after the rout at the bridge he gathered the remnants, fought again, lost again, and when he met Hulü Jin his attempt to persuade him to surrender failed and nearly cost him his life; he was finally bound by his own men and sent to the capital, and two years later was executed. Hulü Jin, famous for refusing to surrender, was one of the few Eastern Wei commanders who kept his formations together in the midst of a lost battle.
kits: 本戰真正上陣的是騎兵裝備。東魏號稱鐵騎，即人著鎧、馬披具裝的騎兵，河北盛產良馬，長於平原衝撞；西魏的精騎同樣以具裝為主，李弼所部用於橫蹙的鐵騎是全戰最硬的一支突擊力量，但總量有限。冷兵器以槊與長矛為主，騎手多執一丈以上的長槊衝陣，近身之後改用直身單刃的環首刀斬擊與砍馬腿；環首刀自漢代以來就是中原刀的主線形制，刀首的環既便於懸掛，也便於回收；此外還有短刀與匕首作副兵器，東魏騎兵用繩索繫刀於鞍後，缺甲時以弓箭、騎槊補戰。防具除網鍪與札甲外，還有騎兵用的各種小盾與護臂。攻城方面，東魏對潼關用過木製撞車一類的器械，關中守軍則以深溝高壘的土木工事與弩機應對，兩軍都曾放火焚燒對方的營壘以斷其薪糧。糧秣方面，關中連年饑荒，守軍靠軍屯與關中倉儲度日；東魏二十萬大軍的糧食需自河東、河北分批運至蒲津，渡船不足又逢六月大雨，軍隊只能涉水而渡，後方接應吃緊。卡面的羅馬短劍出自同期東羅馬帝國，與潼關前線的環首刀同屬短兵器一類，但羅馬自三世紀起以較長的直劍取代短劍配大盾的組合，到查士丁尼一世時短劍更多是禁衛軍的儀仗與副兵器；東魏西魏的近戰靠槊與刀，也不靠盾牆，故此劍並未出現在潼關。
kitsEn: What actually went into this battle was mounted equipment. The Eastern Wei Tied Cavalry rode with armoured men and armoured horses, and the rich horse country of Hebei gave them their strength in the charge across open ground. The Western Wei heavy cavalry was likewise armoured, and the Tied Cavalry under Li Bi, used for the flanking stroke, was the hardest of the striking forces on the field, though its numbers were small. The principal hand weapons were the long spear and the lance; a rider normally carried a spear more than one zhang long and struck from the saddle, switching to the straight, single-edged ring-pommel sabre once he closed, cutting at the enemy and at the horses' legs. The ring-pommel sabre had been the standard Chinese blade since the Han, its ring convenient both for hanging the weapon and for recovering it after a blow. Short knives and daggers served as sidearms; Eastern Wei riders carried their blades on the saddle by a cord and fought with bow and lance when unarmoured. Besides helmets and lamellar armour the cavalry used small shields and arm guards of various kinds. For the siege of Tong Pass the Eastern Wei brought up wooden battering rams, while the defenders answered with deep trenches, high ramparts and crossbows, and both sides at times fired the enemy's camp to cut its firewood and supplies. On logistics, Guanzhong was in famine and the garrison subsisted on military farms and local stores, whereas the food for an Eastern Wei host of two hundred thousand had to be moved in batches from Hedong and Hebei to Pujin; with too few ferries and heavy rain in June the army had to ford the river, and the rear of the column was stretched thin. The Roman short sword on the card belongs to the Eastern Roman Empire of the same years, and although it is of the same family of short weapons as the ring-pommel sabre of Tong Pass, the Romans had been replacing the short sword and large shield combination with a longer straight sword since the third century, and by the reign of Justinian I the short sword was largely a ceremonial and secondary weapon of the imperial guard. The armies of Eastern and Western Wei fought at close quarters with spear and sabre rather than with a wall of shields, so this blade never appeared at Tong Pass.
tactics: 潼關是關中的東門戶，北有黃河，南接秦嶺，關城夾在崤山餘脈之間，道路只容車騎單行通過，任何大軍在此都要拉成長縱隊。東魏的戰法是先以步兵與器械攻關，消耗守軍，再以騎兵爭取關外的渭橋通道；彭樂的先鋒渡過渭橋後逼近西魏本陣，企圖把西魏薄弱的兵力拖入消耗戰。宇文泰的應對是據險深溝高壘，不與硬拼，同時把全部可用精騎集中在一個時機。李弼指出東魏兵眾而西魏兵少，平原對陣必敗，但川谷逼迫之地，只要以鐵騎橫著蹙過去，縱隊被壓在狹窄地形裡就會自己潰散。西魏遂在渭橋南列陣，等東魏前鋒過橋、縱隊拉開、主力湧上之前，遣趙貴先以數百騎接戰試其鋒，再由李弼率鐵騎側擊橫蹙，把東魏行列截成兩段；前一陣擾亂加上正面鐵騎衝擊，東魏前軍回身自相踐踏，隊伍崩解，主力無法展開，潰兵一路拋棄甲冑兵器，連夜退往蒲津。守軍沒有追出太遠，關中糧秣吃緊，追擊的收益不足以抵禦補給與反撲的風險，這是全戰最務實的一個決定。
tacticsEn: Tong Pass was the eastern gateway of Guanzhong, with the Yellow River to the north and the Qinling range to the south, the fortress set between the last spurs of the Xiaoshan and the road so narrow that only a single column of carts and riders could pass, so that any army which came here had to stretch into a long line. The Eastern Wei method was to press the pass with infantry and engines in order to wear the garrison down, and then to seize the crossing of the Wei River outside the pass; Peng Le's vanguard forded the river and pushed up to the Western Wei line in the hope of dragging the thin Western force into a war of attrition. Yuwen Tai's answer was to hold the strong ground with deep trenches and high ramparts rather than to meet the attack head on, and at the same time to gather every heavy rider he had into a single moment. Li Bi pointed out that the Eastern host was many and the Western force few, that a battle on level ground would be lost, but that in ground hemmed in by hills, a stroke of the Tied Cavalry pressed across the line would suffice to break a column squeezed into a narrow space. The Western Wei therefore drew up south of the Wei Bridge and waited: once the Eastern vanguard had crossed and its column had drawn out, and before the main body could deploy, Zhao Gui was sent forward with a few hundred riders to test the enemy, and then Li Bi drove the Tied Cavalry across the front in a flanking stroke that cut the Eastern ranks in two. The confusion of the first contact, added to the impact of the armoured horse, turned the Eastern front against itself; the ranks dissolved, the main body could not deploy, and the fugitives threw away armour and weapons all the way back to Pujin. The defenders did not pursue far: with grain short in Guanzhong, the gain from a long pursuit was smaller than the risk of a counter-stroke, and that was the most practical decision of the day.
data: 兵力方面，東魏高歡西征之眾，通史多記為二十萬，騎兵為其主力；西魏在潼關與渭橋投入的兵，通史記為不足五千，眾不滿五千是當時的說法，兩軍規模相差約四十倍。損失方面，渭橋一戰東魏大潰，棄甲者十餘萬，鎧甲兵器散落滿野；十月沙苑再戰，東魏棄甲士卒八萬，鎧仗十之八被西魏收繳，此戰之後又有一批東魏騎兵將領被俘降，其中包括先鋒彭樂。距離與行程方面，潼關至長安約二百餘里，至洛陽約四百餘里，蒲津渡口在黃河東岸，距潼關約二百餘里；渭橋在渭南縣東，跨渭水而連接關中與東方道路，自關中運往洛陽的車隊必經此線。時間方面，東魏六月西征，七月在潼關與渭橋接戰，十月兵敗沙苑，潼關前的相持約十餘日，關中大饑正是這一年。人物的下場，高歡於547年病卒，高敖曹被俘後於539年遭誅，宇文泰於554年病卒，三人之卒都在這場戰爭之後十數年之內。數字多出自戰報與本紀，帶有明顯的誇張，撰史者亦每每註明未可盡信，引用時宜作量級來看。
dataEn: On numbers, the host Gao Huan took west is recorded in the general histories at two hundred thousand, with cavalry in the majority; the Western Wei force committed at Tong Pass and the Wei Bridge is recorded as fewer than five thousand, the phrase fewer than five thousand being the one then in use, so the two armies differed by something like forty to one. On losses, the Eastern army broke at the bridge and more than a hundred thousand men abandoned their armour, leaving mail and weapons scattered over the field; in the second battle at Shayuan that October, eighty thousand Eastern men threw away their armour and eight tenths of the Eastern armour and weapons were taken by the Western Wei, and a number of Eastern mounted officers were taken prisoner and came over, among them the vanguard commander Peng Le. On distances, Tong Pass lies a little over two hundred li from Chang'an and a little over four hundred from Luoyang; the Pujin ford lies on the east bank of the Yellow River about two hundred li from Tong Pass, and the Wei Bridge stands east of Weinan county, straddling the Wei River on the road that joins Guanzhong with the eastern plains, the road every convoy from Guanzhong to Luoyang had to take. On timing, the Eastern campaign opened in June, the fighting at Tong Pass and the bridge came in July, the second defeat at Shayuan in October, and the stalemate before the pass lasted some ten days and more; the great famine in Guanzhong belongs to this very year. On the fates of the principals, Gao Huan died of illness in 547, Gao Aocao was executed in 539 after his capture, and Yuwen Tai died in 554, all three within a dozen years or so of this war. Most of these figures come from battle reports and annals and carry the usual exaggeration; the chroniclers themselves repeatedly note that they cannot be taken at face value, and they are best read as orders of magnitude.
cause: 北魏在534年一分為二：孝武帝西奔關中投宇文泰，高歡另立孝靜帝遷都鄴城，東魏西魏隔關對立，隨即為河東與洛陽的歸屬開戰。潼關是關中通往河南的孔道，控制它等於控制關中的門戶與東進的跳板；高歡在535至536年已取蒲坂、逼河東，又見關中連年饑荒、西魏新立而人心未定，判定關中虛弱可圖，便傾河北之兵西征，志在直取長安，一舉解決北方的分裂。宇文泰一方則必須守住關中這唯一的屏障：長安本身無險可依，一旦潼關與渭橋失守，關中平原便無險可守，關隴集團與剛剛建立起來的軍屯、府兵都會失去根基；同時關中饑荒使任何一支深入的大軍都難以就地取糧，防守方反而佔了持久戰的便宜。於是雙方在潼關外形成一種必然的結局：進攻方要在縱隊還沒有拉開時一次打穿，防守方要在狹窄地形裡把對手的縱隊壓扁。
causeEn: The Northern Wei split in two in 534: Emperor Xiaowu fled west to Guanzhong and placed himself in the hands of Yuwen Tai, while Gao Huan set up Emperor Xiaojing and moved the capital to Ye, and the two successor states stood opposite each other across the passes and went to war over the ownership of Hedong and Luoyang. Tong Pass was the road out of Guanzhong toward Henan, and whoever held it held both the doorway of Guanzhong and the springboard for an advance eastward. Gao Huan had already taken Puban and pressed into Hedong in 535 and 536, and when he saw the repeated famine in Guanzhong and the new and unsettled Western Wei, he judged the region hollow and attacked, pouring the troops of Hebei westward with the aim of taking Chang'an in one stroke and settling the division of the north at once. The Western Wei had to keep this one barrier: Chang'an has no natural defence of its own, and once Tong Pass and the Wei Bridge were lost the plain of Guanzhong could be entered freely, and both the Guanzhong military group and the military farms and garrison system just then being built would lose their foundation. The famine in Guanzhong also meant that any deep-penetrating army would find it hard to feed itself on the spot, which in practice favoured the defenders in a war of endurance. What followed at the pass was thus a foregone conclusion in form: the attacker had to break through in one stroke before his column could unfold, and the defender had to crush that column by squeezing it in narrow ground.
impact: 潼關守住之後，關中的安全問題暫時解除，西魏得以把重心放到關中、涼州的軍屯與關隴集團的整編上，柱國與大將分統各部的制度也在這幾年定型，八柱國、十二大將的名制由此成形，這批關隴將門最終成為隋唐兩代的皇族骨架。高敖曹被俘、彭樂被俘降，東魏一時折了最驍勇的兩名騎將，北方兩個政權的力量對比出現變化，東魏的攻勢從此被推回河東，拉鋸的重心轉向洛陽與豫州，此後數十年雙方在洛陽一帶反覆爭奪，直至550年西魏迎孝武帝靈柩入洛陽，554年宇文泰病逝、557年北周代魏，北齊與北周在中原的對峙格局完全定型。戰亂與饑荒也擾動了關外的世界：河套與河西的商旅在兵荒馬亂中斷了絲路，北涼與吐谷渾趁勢擴張，到554年關中再度大饑、戶口流散，大量關中漢人避入河西與巴蜀，陝西與山西的民眾被戰爭反覆抽乾，這些都成了之後隋朝得以整合南北的底色之一。
impactEn: Once Tong Pass was held, the security of Guanzhong was settled for the time being, and the Western Wei was free to give its weight to the military farms in Guanzhong and Liangzhou and to the organisation of the Guanzhong group; the system in which pillar lords and generals each commanded a corps was fixed during these years, and the famous roster of eight pillar lords and twelve generals took its shape here. Those Guanzhong households became the skeleton of the imperial families of the Sui and the Tang. The capture of Gao Aocao and of Peng Le cost the Eastern Wei its two most famous riders and shifted the balance between the two northern states; the Eastern offensive was pushed back to Hedong, and the centre of the contest moved to Luoyang and Yu Province, which the two states fought over for decades, until in 550 the Western Wei brought the remains of Emperor Xiaowu to Luoyang, and after Yuwen Tai died in 554 and the Northern Zhou replaced the Wei in 557, the standoff between Northern Qi and Northern Zhou was fully fixed. War and famine also disturbed the world outside the pass: the merchants of the Hexi corridor and of the Ordos saw the silk road cut by the fighting, Northern Liang and the Tuyuhun expanded at the time, and when Guanzhong was struck by famine again in 554 and the population fled, large numbers of Han households of Guanzhong moved into Hexi and into Bashu, and the populations of Shaanxi and Shanxi were drained again and again by the war. All of this became part of the groundwork that later allowed the Sui to unite north and south.
result: 西魏守住了潼關與渭橋，東魏大軍在關外受挫退回：高歡退回鄴城整頓河北，數年內不敢再大舉深入；被俘的高敖曹在次年被誅，量才之將折損東魏元氣，十月沙苑再敗，鎧仗十之八落入西魏之手，兩戰連擊之後東魏的西征計劃徹底失敗。西魏則以數千精騎擊潰二十萬大軍，士氣與戰略名望都推到頂點。勝負不在人數而在指揮：進攻方把二十萬人塞進一條狹窄通道，防守方把全部騎兵壓在橫蹙的一擊上，兩相比較，關中無險可守的說法第一次被打斷。但代價也在西魏這邊：關中饑荒未解，軍屯成為唯一支柱，一旦戰事拖延，糧秣仍舊吃緊；高歡的西征也在客觀上替西魏贏得整頓軍制的時間。此戰之後，東西魏的疆界仍大致以河東與潼關為界，真正改變天下的是接下來十年間洛陽的爭奪，而不是這一天的潼關。
resultEn: The Western Wei held Tong Pass and the Wei Bridge, and the Eastern army broke up outside and withdrew: Gao Huan returned to Ye, set his house in order in Hebei, and for years did not dare attempt a deep penetration again. Gao Aocao was executed the following year, and the loss of such a talent darkened the Eastern Wei's prospects; the second defeat at Shayuan in October, with eight tenths of the armour taken, ended the Eastern campaign plan outright. The Western Wei, on the other hand, had beaten an army of two hundred thousand with a few thousand heavy riders, and its morale and renown in the art of war reached a peak. The victory lay not in numbers but in command: the attacker packed two hundred thousand men into a narrow channel while the defender concentrated every rider into one flanking stroke, and the claim that Guanzhong was indefensible was broken for the first time. The cost fell on the Western side as well. The famine in Guanzhong was not relieved, military farms became the only pillar of supply, and if the war dragged on the grain would remain short. Gao Huan's western march had also bought the Western Wei the time it needed to put its military system in order. After this the boundary between the two states still ran roughly along Hedong and Tong Pass, and what really changed the shape of the realm was the struggle over Luoyang in the ten years that followed, not this single day at the pass.
